stories.title: Chennai designers repurpose saris
stories.summary: Repurposing fabric was a domestic practice long before sustainability became a buzzword. By 2017, the trend found a niche footing in Chennai, with designers reimagining old saris as contemporary ensembles. The life of a garment rarely ends, provided it is not in the kitchen as a cleaning cloth.

stories.title: Haryana courts Surat textile firms for Sohna township
stories.summary: Haryana is pitching its 1,600-acre IMT Sohna industrial township to Surat textile entrepreneurs. The state aims to connect Gujarat manufacturers with NCR apparel markets. The city exported textiles and garments worth 15,104 crore rupees in 2025-26, ranking as the country's fourth-largest exporting district in the category.

stories.title: Festive sales defy gloom with double-digit growth
stories.summary: Festive sales in October crossed 1.5 trillion rupees, with e-commerce majors witnessing a 25 percent uptick. Physical retail also registered unexpected double-digit growth. Industry analysts noted that while consumption was high, the season remained nuanced as some categories faced headwinds due to pricing and availability.

stories.title: Nykaa reports profit in fashion vertical
stories.summary: Nykaa reported a 27 percent year-on-year revenue growth for its beauty vertical in the second quarter of fiscal 2027. The company's fashion business recorded its third consecutive quarter of EBITDA-level profitability. The firm continues to seek a clear differentiator for its fashion segment.

stories.title: HUL increases detergent prices
stories.summary: Hindustan Unilever has hiked the maximum retail price of several detergent products by up to 11 percent. Price jumps range from 1 to 10 rupees across various pack sizes. A one-kilogram pack of Surf Excel Quick Wash is now 10 rupees more expensive.

stories.title: Gold jewellery stolen in Coimbatore
stories.summary: Unidentified individuals stole 23 sovereigns of gold jewellery from a residence in Coimbatore. The homeowner discovered the theft on November 7, after returning from a wedding and storing the items in a bedroom cupboard. Police are investigating the missing bangles, earrings, bracelets, and cuffs.

stories.title: Online fashion orders spread across marketplaces
stories.summary: The combined market share of Myntra and Flipkart declined by 12.2 percentage points as orders spread across more platforms. Transactions below 1,000 rupees accounted for half of all sales, while promotional discounts averaged 46 percent. Deepening discounts remain the primary driver for festive-season volume.

stories.title: BlueStone reports 45 percent festive growth
stories.summary: BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Limited reported 45 percent year-on-year business growth between October 1 and November 8. The retailer attributed the expansion to an increase in the number of buyers, noting that average realisations remained unchanged compared to the same period last year.

stories.title: Frontier Raas expands to Ahmedabad
stories.summary: Frontier Raas has opened a new retail store in Ahmedabad, featuring bridalwear and handloom saris. Actor Kangana Ranaut attended the inauguration of the outlet on November 1. Established in 1954, the brand continues to focus on traditional Indian craftsmanship and occasionwear.

stories.title: Kareena Kapoor wears royal heirlooms for Diwali
stories.summary: Kareena Kapoor paired a silver kaftan and turban with 200-year-old jewellery for Diwali. The outfit included a kalgi that once belonged to the Nawab of Bhopal and a 30-carat emerald. The look was designed to evoke royalty, complete with accessories that have seen more history than the wearer.

stories.title: Global buyers flock to South Korea for fashion
stories.summary: Korean fashion brands, which once traveled globally to find stockists, are now hosting international buyers at home. Brand managers from Japan and China recently gathered at the Pangyo Digital Center to preview 2027 spring collections. The tables have turned for brands that spent years persuading managers.

stories.title: Ghana hosts maiden Black Star Fashion Week
stories.summary: The inaugural Black Star Fashion Week concluded with a Presidential Runway at the Royal Senchi Hotel. The event featured collections from leading Ghanaian designers, aiming to position the country as a destination for creative enterprise. The runway celebrated local heritage, craftsmanship, and the ambition of the industry.

stories.title: Alero Ebigbeyi shifts focus to affordable fashion
stories.summary: After three decades creating luxury pieces for high-end clientele, designer Alero Ebigbeyi is redirecting her expertise toward the inclusive market. The London College of Fashion graduate aims to challenge the perception that quality fashion must come at a premium price through her brand, Heych.

stories.title: Luxury brands release festive campaigns
stories.summary: Gucci, Tommy Hilfiger, Mackage, Louis Vuitton, Etro, and Ami have unveiled their respective campaigns for the festive season. The full details of these marketing initiatives are available for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: LATAM Luxury Summit explores hospitality and design
stories.summary: The LATAM Luxury Summit 2026 brought together Latin American designers and Hyatt Inclusive Collection resorts in Mexico City. The event focused on the evolving definition of luxury through cultural identity and hospitality. The program featured industry discussions, destination presentations, and a runway show.

stories.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga preserves heritage through natural dyes
stories.summary: Zimbabwean designer Nkanyeziyethu Malunga uses plants and tree bark to create natural dyes for her fabric collections. Her work aims to make indigenous knowledge visible while demonstrating its potential for future commercial activities. Each material used in her Bulawayo workshop carries its own history of preparation.

stories.title: Skirts return to the 2026 fashion cycle
stories.summary: Skirts are appearing in every shape and length across recent runways, from Prada to various fall collections. The garment has historically carried the weight of social conventions and political debate. Fashion is currently attempting to rewrite the rules, though the skirt remains a symbol of self-expression.

stories.title: GIA acquires large collection of rare and unusual gemstones
stories.summary: The Gemological Institute of America has acquired 2,665 crystals and minerals featuring unusual inclusions like trapped fluids and fluorescent petroleum. The collection was curated over 60 years by analytical microscopist John Koivula. The institute now holds a significant record of what usually stays inside a stone.

stories.title: Pink diamonds and royal jewellery lead upcoming auctions
stories.summary: Sotheby’s will host two auctions in Geneva on November 11, featuring an 8.63-carat fancy-intense-pink diamond expected to fetch 6 million dollars. The sales will include high jewellery and royal items. The market for historic aristocratic accessories remains active.

stories.summary: Bibi van der Velden has launched its first high jewellery line, the Eclipse collection, featuring an alligator motif rendered in diamonds and spinels. The brand describes the pieces as its most refined exploration of diamonds to date. The reptiles are now available in two abstract suites.

stories.title: Oscar Heyman’s rose-cut sapphire bracelet
stories.summary: Oscar Heyman has released a platinum and 18k gold bracelet featuring multicolored rose-cut sapphires and round diamonds. Priced at 150,000 dollars, the piece uses a scatter-like setting for its stones. The brand suggests that rose-cut coloured gemstones offer an entirely new experience.

stories.title: Chopard’s most glamorous era gets a brilliant revival
stories.summary: Chopard is touring a vintage exhibition titled L’Heure du Diamant, featuring archival jewellery watches with tiger’s-eye and lapis lazuli dials. The collection has visited Geneva, Dubai, Cannes and Paris. The house is now bringing its history of watchmaking to the United States.

stories.title: Jaeger-LeCoultre releases vintage collection in New York
stories.summary: Jaeger-LeCoultre has launched "The Collectibles VIII" on Madison Avenue, featuring nine historical watches produced between 1933 and 1981. The curation targets the American market, highlighting a period when the Swiss watchmaker navigated mid-century tariffs. Enthusiasts can now acquire these museum-grade timepieces directly from the brand.

stories.title: Casio shrinks A168 watch into a ring
stories.summary: Casio is releasing a stainless steel ring watch based on its A168 model. The device features a module one-tenth the standard size to power an LCD, stopwatch, calendar and hourly Time Flash. Silver and gold versions arrive in Japan this month, with no international launch date confirmed.

stories.title: The Traveling Penny opens second store in Columbia
stories.summary: Greenville-based jewelry brand The Traveling Penny has opened a permanent location in Columbia’s Five Points District. The store features a "charm bar" for custom necklaces and bracelets. Despite the name, the brand says it is here to stay after operating a pop-up in the area.

stories.title: NABARD launches Stall in Mall initiative
stories.summary: NABARD has inaugurated "Stall in Mall" outlets at PVP Square Mall in Vijayawada to provide market access for rural artisans. Regional Chief General Manager Somender Singh stated the initiative aims to provide modern marketing opportunities for traditional handloom and handicraft products through partnerships with local foundations.

stories.title: New book explores modern Mexican interiors
stories.summary: Writer Su Wu has released "Mesoamerican Modern," a book featuring 16 Mexican homes that incorporate pre-Hispanic architectural traditions. Photographer Luis Garvan captured the interiors, which Wu describes as a departure from the museum-like preservation of artifacts. The project focuses on the presence of ancient ideas in contemporary spaces.

stories.title: Study explores 3D-printed textiles as leather alternatives
stories.summary: A study published in Fashion and Textiles explores using 3D printing to replicate crocodile, snake and zebra skins. Researchers used common thermoplastic materials to create flexible structures, aiming to address the environmental impact of the leather tanning industry. The method focuses on reducing water consumption and hazardous chemical use.

stories.title: Textile competitiveness requires more than low costs
stories.summary: An analysis presented at the ITMF Annual Conference suggests India’s textile competitiveness depends on supply chain efficiency, technology adoption and policy certainty. While tariffs may help attract export orders, the report notes that retaining buyers requires improvements beyond factory-level production costs. Delivery timelines remain a critical factor for growth.

stories.title: WonderLab hosts fashion sustainability event
stories.summary: The WonderLab Science Museum recently hosted a "Stitched & Salvaged" event to teach attendees about fashion sustainability. Partnering with Discardia, the museum provided hands-on sewing activities to repurpose damaged clothing. The program, funded by a philanthropic sorority, aimed to demonstrate the importance of reuse to younger attendees.

stories.title: COP31 addresses fashion industry pollution
stories.summary: The COP31 climate conference in Turkey is focusing on environmental impacts, including the fashion industry's status as a major global polluter. The event aims to secure commitments on clean energy and fossil fuel reduction. The industry is under pressure to limit consumption and waste during the two-week summit.

stories.title: Resale platforms face potential under-16 ban
stories.summary: The UK government is considering whether a proposed social media ban for under-16s should include online marketplaces like eBay, Vinted and Depop. Regulators are debating the boundary between shopping and social networking, as these platforms often rely on personalised feeds and messaging features to facilitate peer-to-peer sales.

stories.title: SMALLrevolution wins design prize for recycled furniture
stories.summary: SMALLrevolution placed second in the designboom special prize at the Seoul Design Award 2026 for its traceable recycling systems. The company turns recycled aircraft safety strips into furniture, aiming to make the material's history visible. The project focuses on circular innovation to address 21st-century plastic waste.

stories.title: Botswana to increase stake in De Beers
stories.summary: Botswana has agreed to double its stake in De Beers to 30 percent. The move clears a path for Anglo American to exit its ownership of the diamond producer. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.summary: Perry Ellis International has appointed Liz Rodbell as group president. The company manages a portfolio of fashion brands. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Calvin Klein parts ways with Veronica Leoni
stories.summary: Calvin Klein has ended its relationship with designer Veronica Leoni following her Fall 2026 collection. Leoni joined the brand in 2024 to relaunch its collection, but her recent work received critical reviews. The brand is currently searching for a successor in the ongoing cycle of designer turnover.

stories.title: Dior holiday campaign faces AI accusations
stories.summary: Dior is facing claims that its latest holiday campaign utilised artificial intelligence, despite the luxury house advertising the work as handmade. The incident has prompted questions regarding the definition of craftsmanship in luxury marketing, as brands increasingly rely on digital tools to produce content that mimics traditional artisan techniques.

stories.summary: Lululemon has announced new appointments to its C-suite under the leadership of Heidi O'Neill. The company is restructuring its executive team. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.summary: Morgan Stanley and Jefferies have both set a 415-euro price target for LVMH, with neither firm recommending a buy. Analysts cited concerns over demand, leading to a slight decline in the stock price. The market is currently testing the luxury group's ability to maintain growth.

stories.summary: Botswana will increase its holding in De Beers to 30 percent. The agreement is part of a broader transition regarding the ownership of the diamond company. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Euratex and Global Fashion Agenda form alliance
stories.summary: The European Apparel and Textile Confederation and Global Fashion Agenda have formed a strategic alliance to coordinate policy agendas and sustainability efforts. The organizations aim to advocate for legislation that balances ambition with workability, ensuring that on-the-ground implementation across the textile value chain is actually possible.

stories.title: Martine Rose named creative director at Balenciaga
stories.summary: Kering has appointed Martine Rose as the new creative director of Balenciaga, succeeding Pierpaolo Piccioli. CEO Luca de Meo stated the move supports the house's ambition to remain at the forefront of innovation, creativity, and culture. The appointment marks a new creative phase for the brand.

Launched in 2024, the award celebrates contemporary Chinese design with a focus on sustainable development and cultural dialogue. The winning projects explore architecture, jewellery, furniture, lighting, and graphic design.

A beautiful collection does not guarantee success without the right customers.
